sources.title: Michael Weiskopf, Cappadocia, Encyclopaedia Iranica (1990)
sources.note: Direct scholarly entry read. Post-Achaemenid kingdom, administrative landscape, Hellenization and resources sections. Avoided incorrect numbering/chronology in secondary snippets elsewhere; Roman annexation 17 CE explicit. Specific family/education facts restricted to ruling houses.

sources.title: Mary M. Voigt, Celts at Gordion: The Late Hellenistic Settlement (2003), Penn Museum Expedition
sources.note: Original archaeologist report read via full indexed original. Household artifacts, construction, immigrant-family interpretation, workshop complex. Its early interpretation of Deserted Village chronology checked against newer Digital Gordion; no outdated single-phase inference or gender-essentialist blue-pigment joke repeated.

sources.title: Penn Museum Digital Gordion, Hellenistic Gordion
sources.note: Direct excavation-project synthesis read. Lines 143-153: three Galatian phases, ca.150-100 BCE reoccupation, artifact assemblages, houses/courtyards and mismatched pottery. Separate work from Voigt 2003; former report facts remain allocated to that report. No universal Galatian practice inferred.

sources.title: M. L. Chaumont, Armenia and Iran II: The pre-Islamic period, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Original scholarly entry indexed text checked on Artaxias city foundation and boundary stones; fuller politics includes Tigranes. Existing Armenia narrative uses same URL; cumulative budget counted. Hannibal foundation story explicitly doubted by author, not adopted.

sources.title: James R. Russell, Artaxias I, Encyclopaedia Iranica (1986)
sources.note: Direct original scholarly entry lines 35-37, Aramaic boundary-stone transliteration MLK RWNDKN, alternative reading noted, gloss Orontid king. Existing Armenia card uses this work and quote; cumulative paraphrase and quotation counted. Article has erroneous Magnesia date, excluded.

sources.title: British Museum, Cappadocian silver drachm 1979,0101.1040
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue: Ariarathes VII, approximately116-101 BCE, minted Caesarea Mazaca, silver4.18g, head with diadem, Athena holds Nike. Inscription field not accessible, so no Greek text guessed from this record.

proposedOverrides.name: Minor states of Anatolia and Armenia
proposedOverrides.summary: A broad atlas umbrella across Anatolian and Armenian regions in the last two centuries BCE, with distinct kingdoms, households and political trajectories.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone regional umbrella, not shared with either other target
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Includes Gordium/Ancyra/Amaseia/Mazaka/Artaxata/Garni; excludes Pergamon/Sardis/Sinope/Samosata/Nemrut. Broad footprint does not demonstrate political control. Related named states remain distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Archaeological household examples are from Gordion, political examples from Cappadocia and Armenia. No medical protocol, universal school system or household sanitation generalized to the entire region.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Aramaic boundary inscription represented only by source-verified scholarly transliteration; no guessed original letters. Existing Armenia source reuse counted.
